cb9f6aeb096e.exp: With way ahead, putting the tiller to starboard takes the rudder blade to port; the water pushes the stern to starboard and the bow falls off to port. Rule: the tiller is put to the side opposite to where we want the bow to go, and the blade goes toward the side of the turn.

96b263fc8e7a.exp: You approach the buoy with the bow into the wind (or into the current if it dominates), because that way the wind slows the way and lets you control the approach and stop beside the buoy. With the wind astern the boat would be pushed along and hard to stop.

f85241070152.exp: Set (deriva) is the displacement that the current causes in the vessel's track. Not to be confused with leeway (abatimiento), which is the effect of the wind on the topsides and is measured as the angle between the heading and the track due to the wind.

052fec8c4ad7.exp: Steerage speed (velocidad de gobierno) is the minimum at which the boat obeys the rudder, because the blade needs sufficient water flow to act. Below it the boat does not steer. Cruising speed is the usual sailing speed, not the minimum steerage speed.

f5566e3ee50c.exp: To coil the lines (adujar) is to gather them in orderly turns, so they are ready to be cast off without knots or tangles when mooring again. To ease (lascar) is to let go a little, to take up tension (templar) is to tighten, and to heave (virar) is to turn or haul in.

3243a5e82b1d.exp: The stern line (codera) is the mooring line taken to a firm point farther away, on the side opposite the quay (a buoy or another quay), and serves to help when leaving the berth and to keep the boat away. Springs and head lines go to the quay itself, not on the opposite side.

31c49543c808.exp: When mooring bows- or stern-to (amarre de punta), the lines that run diagonally toward the bottom on the opposite side, to buoys or mooring blocks, which keep the boat away from the quay and aligned, are called coderas. They are not head lines or springs, which belong to alongside berthing.

52c3aafd7dc7.exp: When leaving a berth you normally cast off the stern first, separate the stern from the quay, go astern with the engine and finally cast off at the bow. That way the bow, which is still secured, acts as a pivot and prevents the stern or propeller touching the quay. Casting off the bow lines first would force the stern toward the quay, the opposite of what is wanted.

e886d4b9dcf2.exp: Inside the harbour you manoeuvre at steerage speed (velocidad de gobierno): the minimum at which the boat still obeys the rudder. This reduces the risk of damage and of wash to other craft. Maximum or cruising speed are excessive, and there is no fixed value of 3 knots as a rule.

e129b0157eef.exp: With a right-handed propeller (dextrógira, turns clockwise going ahead), going astern it turns counter-clockwise and the paddle-wheel effect pushes the stern to port. Mnemonic: right-handed astern, stern to port; the effect appears above all when starting from rest.

993f9deb98eb.exp: The left-handed propeller (levógira) turns counter-clockwise ahead and clockwise astern, and in that direction the lower blades push the stern to starboard. It is the opposite effect to the right-handed one, which takes the stern to port.

47ff75b9f44f.exp: With a right-handed propeller going astern, the propeller effect takes the stern to port. If we also put the rudder to port, the blade, pushed by the water arriving from astern, also takes the stern to port. The two effects add up: the stern goes quickly to port and the bow falls off quickly to starboard.

033a7e4ff9b3.exp: With way ahead, for the bow to fall off to starboard the tiller is put to port: the blade turns to starboard, pushes the stern to port and the bow falls off to starboard. Rule: tiller to the side opposite to where we want to fall off (blade to the side toward which we want to go).

a7d2b13d4321.exp: When berthing with the bow spring made fast to the quay, a little engine ahead and the rudder to the side away from the quay, the boat advances, pivots on the spring and the stern comes toward the quay in a controlled way. It is done with the bow spring because, with this line fast, engine ahead closes the boat against the quay.

3f62c525fcb4.exp: To haul in (cobrar) is to pull a line and gather it in. To pay out and to ease (arriar and lascar) are to slacken or let it go (the opposite), and to make fast (hacer firme) is to secure it definitively to a fixed point.

2d1bc495c846.exp: To stopper (abozar) is to temporarily hold a line with another of smaller diameter (mena, thickness), called a stopper (boza), for example to relieve the strain of a line under load while it is made fast. To tighten (azocar) is to pull a knot tight and to furl (aferrar) is to secure or gather sails.

7ed02a8ca95f.exp: Moored alongside, the line that keeps the boat away from the quay and prevents her from knocking is the codera. Head lines and springs prevent the boat from moving ahead or astern, not from moving away or toward the quay.

c5dc57dd73b9.exp: Moored alongside, the line that keeps the boat away from the quay and prevents knocks against it is the codera. The breast line holds transversely but pulls the side toward the quay, and the head lines and springs control longitudinal movement.

8ef887d4806f.exp: The stern spring (esprín de popa) runs from the stern forward. By its direction it restrains the boat so she does not move forward, just like the bow line, which also pulls forward. That is why it is said to be analogous to the bow line; the bow spring would be the analogue of the stern line.

01558c0c7591.exp: To moor to a buoy you head into the wind, so that the wind slows the way. With a south wind (which comes from 180 degrees) you must sail with the bow toward the south, that is, on course 180.

d3334349ffa3.exp: You head into the wind to moor to a buoy. A north-easterly wind comes from 045 degrees, so the course, with the bow facing where it blows from, is 045. Course 225 would be with the wind astern.

a919c3374872.exp: To haul in (cobrar) is to gather by pulling; the opposite action, with the line under load, is to pay out (filar: letting it go gradually, with control). To hoist (izar) is to raise something, to coil (adujar) is to gather in an orderly way and to luff up (orzar) is to bring the bow toward the wind.

07f5b3f2b67f.exp: The agents that condition manoeuvring are wind, current and swell, because they are external forces that deflect or slow the boat. Sunshine and relative humidity are meteorological factors that do not affect the vessel's movement.

74dbdbdfbc40.exp: When gathering lines you coil them (adujar): they are wound in orderly turns, so that they can later run freely without tangles. Casting them off or taking turns does not put them in order.

59f153977397.exp: To ease (lascar) is to let go or slacken a little a line that is working (under tension). To pull it and gather it is to haul in (cobrar), and to gather it by winding it on itself is to coil (adujar).

d332cf2a6510.exp: To turn around (ciabogar) is to turn or swing a vessel in the smallest possible space, which is normal in a harbour manoeuvre. It is not putting the bow into the wind (luffing up or heaving to) nor dragging the anchor (garrear).

f46048bf747f.exp: To ease a line (lascar) is to slacken it a little when it is working. It is not making fast (taking turns around a mooring fitting), nor securing it with knots, nor putting it in order, which is coiling (adujar).

de61a868aea1.exp: To coil (adujar) is to wind a line in orderly turns (aduja) to stow it, preventing it from tangling. Securing it to a fixed point is making fast (hacer firme) or mooring, and cutting it has no specific name in this operation.

d4bf5b378e73.exp: To haul in a line (cobrar) is to pull on it and gather it aboard. It does not mean to make it fast, to take turns with it or to take it out of the water. The opposite is to pay out or ease off (filar or arriar).

1f527a4fad0b.exp: With a current from astern, to open the stern when leaving the berth, the bow spring is left as the last line. Going gently ahead with the rudder toward the quay, the boat pivots on that spring and the stern separates from the quay. The stern spring would open the bow, not the stern.

bf0214b5614e.exp: With a wind from ahead, the boat tends to go astern, and the lines that restrain her are those pointing forward from the boat: the bow line and the stern spring. The stern line and the bow spring work the other way, so they do not counter this wind.

e911633ec5f2.exp: With a wind from astern, the bow spring made fast makes the boat pivot on the bow when going ahead with the rudder toward the quay, and the stern opens away from the quay. The stern lines would hold the stern rather than open it.

3e06fa8e5ec5.exp: To open the stern when leaving a berth with a wind from astern, the bow spring is used: being the last line, the boat pivots on the bow and the stern moves away from the quay. The stern lines would hold the stern rather than open it.

d2eab77e0482.exp: With a wind from ahead, to open the bow the stern spring is left fast: the boat pivots on the stern and the wind, which arrives from the bow, pushes it outward. It is the symmetrical case to a wind from astern, which is solved with the bow spring.

21f85ecfb48c.exp: With a wind from ahead, the boat tends to go astern and to open her bow, so the long lines must be reinforced, which are the ones that bear the longitudinal strain, both bow and stern. The codera is not used in an alongside (abarloado) berth.

3516f68b6020.exp: With two engines and no current, you turn around (ciabogar) with the rudder amidships: it is enough to put one engine ahead and the other astern for the boat to turn on the spot. The rudder is not necessary, and putting it to one side would slow the turn. That is why option b is not correct.

04ccc83c354c.exp: To pick up a buoy you approach with the wind ahead (or the current ahead), because that way the wind slows the way and lets you control speed and stop right at the buoy. With the wind astern the boat would be pushed along and hard to stop.

20e767d96e94.exp: The right-handed propeller (dextrógira) turns clockwise ahead; going astern it turns counter-clockwise, and the paddle-wheel effect takes the stern to port. Even if the rudder is amidships, the propeller effect exists, especially when starting from rest.

50782b8a270c.exp: When going astern, the stern falls toward the side to which the blades turn in their upper part (paddle-wheel effect). If the propeller is right-handed, going astern it turns counter-clockwise and the stern goes to port; if left-handed, to starboard. So it is not the same either way.

99e7870e776c.exp: Right-handed propeller astern: the propeller turns counter-clockwise, and through the paddle-wheel effect the stern falls to port. It is the classic rule for berthing manoeuvres with the boat stopped, where the effect is more pronounced as there is no way on.

0220d80315e3.exp: A propeller that turns clockwise when going astern is left-handed (levógira) (it turns counter-clockwise going ahead). With the engine astern, the paddle-wheel effect takes the stern to starboard. Right-handed astern: stern to port; left-handed astern: stern to starboard.

feea95cfc1eb.exp: A propeller that turns counter-clockwise when going astern is right-handed (dextrógira) (it turns clockwise going ahead). With the engine astern the paddle-wheel effect takes the stern to port. The turning of the propeller does affect the direction, above all with the boat stopped.

2c8c2fec270d.exp: After an unintentional grounding (varada), the first thing is to assess: check the nature of the bottom (sand, mud, rock) and possible damage or leaks in the hull, before trying to get off. Going astern immediately could worsen the damage or leave a leak open.

e51dd4dadf6d.exp: You abandon ship only when she offers less safety than any other means of survival, such as the liferaft. As long as the boat floats she is the best refuge: she is more visible, larger and safer than the raft.

a95b93170cf8.exp: For urgent medical consultations at sea, contact the Radio-Medical Centre (Centro Radio-Médico) of the Instituto Social de la Marina (CRME), which gives medical assistance to vessels 24 hours a day. The Guardia Civil, the Harbour Master or a clinic do not offer radio-medical assistance.

a533599dbf78.exp: On the hard (varadero), to prevent flooding, check the points where water can enter the hull: the seacocks, the shaft tube (bocina, passage of the propeller shaft) and the rudder trunk (limera, passage of the rudder stock). Anchors, engine or sails are not water entry points.

322763fd9870.exp: The rudder trunk (limera) is the opening through which the rudder stock (mecha) passes through the hull; it is a risk point for leaks. Not to be confused with the shaft tube (bocina), through which the propeller shaft passes, nor with the scupper (imbornal, deck drain) or the hawse pipe (gatera, passage of the anchor line).

066337187d19.exp: The basic fire-fighting procedures are to locate the fire, confine it (isolate it by closing vents and doors) and extinguish it. You start by knowing where it is and preventing it from spreading, before attacking it.

6cda8c84fed4.exp: If there are several people in the water with lifejackets, it is best to huddle together: this preserves body heat, boosts morale and makes the group more visible to rescue teams. Taking off lifejackets or warm clothing is counterproductive: buoyancy and heat are lost.

4ba289f81721.exp: The Spanish Radio-Medical Centre (Centro Radio-Médico Español) handles urgent consultations 24 hours a day, every day of the year. For non-urgent consultations there is a recommended, more limited schedule.

f485da86df87.exp: Before establishing communication with the radio-doctor you must have ready the patient's details and the symptoms that prompt the consultation, in order to give clear and quick information. The service is free of charge and requires no subscription.

a8ee396b487e.exp: With the engine stopped and the boat berthed, the seacock is closed to prevent a leak: if a hose or fitting fails with the valve open, water enters the boat. It has nothing to do with fuel, and the stopped engine no longer needs cooling.

077a0510d6ae.exp: Smothering (sofocación) puts out the fire by eliminating the oxidiser, that is, oxygen. Lowering the temperature is cooling, stopping the reaction is inhibition and diluting or removing the fuel is dispersion or isolation.

451c1e570338.exp: Flares are shown to leeward so that smoke and sparks do not come toward us or burn us. To windward they would be blown back against the boat or the person.

8dedd6964558.exp: Venous blood returns to the heart: it is dark red and flows continuously, without pulsing. Arterial blood is bright red and spurts in time with the heartbeat. Mnemonic: artery bright and spurting; vein dark and continuous.

69099afc62f9.exp: The order to abandon ship is given when the vessel offers less safety than other means of survival (the raft). As long as the boat floats, she is the best refuge; abandoning her earlier is a mistake.

0c2502420ce1.exp: By putting the stern to the wind and sailing at the wind's speed, the apparent wind is zero: the flames and smoke are not fanned nor driven toward the crew. Bow to the wind would fan the fire, since it would add the boat's speed to the wind's.

6d28b37e6497.exp: In an engine fire the first thing is to stop the engine and cut off the fuel supply and the electrical contact, to remove the fuel and the ignition source. Do not open the hatch (oxygen would enter) nor throw water on a fuel or electrical fire.

9b533fceb244.exp: The shaft tube (bocina) is the opening through which the propeller shaft passes through the hull and is a point vulnerable to leaks. The rudder trunk (limera) is the equivalent for the rudder shaft, and scuppers and hawse pipes are other deck fittings.

736d6c5e3da3.exp: Arterial blood leaves the heart under pressure: it is bright red and spurts (pulsating) following the heartbeat. Venous blood is dark and continuous. Mnemonic: artery bright and spurting.

8c641c980de0.exp: In external bleeding from a limb, you press directly on the wound and raise the limb. The tourniquet is the last resort, only if the bleeding cannot be stopped. Hot water would increase the bleeding.

ee02be903dd7.exp: Most collisions are due to human error and failure to comply with the COLREGs: lack of look-out, excessive speed or wrong manoeuvres. Efficient look-out, safe speed and correct stowage are measures that prevent collisions, not their causes.

4b1fffd8adfe.exp: For a first-degree sunburn (reddened skin), the person is protected from the sun and moisturising cream or aftersun is applied. Blisters are not drained because of the risk of infection, the person is not wrapped up or made to sweat, and salt water is no use.

91ef7fb303f8.exp: Smothering (sofocación) puts out the fire by eliminating oxygen (the oxidiser), for example with a fire blanket, foam or CO2. Removing the fuel is dispersion and breaking the chain reaction is inhibition.

8e1435f7a389.exp: The HELP position consists of drawing the legs up over the stomach and holding them with the arms, protecting the areas of greatest heat loss (groin, armpits, chest). It is adopted with a lifejacket to delay hypothermia; moving about in the water increases heat loss.

bd82e773bd90.exp: Putting the stern to the wind and sailing at its speed cancels the apparent wind, so the flames and smoke are not fanned nor driven toward the crew. With the bow into the wind, the apparent wind would be greater and would fan the fire.

cb55bb112152.exp: After an unintentional grounding (varada), first the nature of the bottom and possible hull damage are analysed, before trying to get free. Going astern immediately may worsen the damage or open a leak.

597c51557ecd.exp: Venous bleeding is dark red blood that flows continuously. Arterial is bright red and spurting, following the pulse. Mnemonic: vein dark and continuous.

04647a9b0794.exp: Water on a class A fire (solids) acts by cooling, lowering the temperature of the fuel, and by smothering, by forming steam that displaces oxygen. That is why it is said to extinguish by cooling and smothering.

086c45d49c63.exp: Seacocks must be opened and closed frequently so that they do not seize up from encrustation or corrosion and remain operational when they need to be closed in an emergency. Leaving them always open or half open would jam them.

357c09bca682.exp: Class A fire is produced by solid fuels (wood, paper, fabrics). Class B: liquids; C: gases; D: metals; F: cooking oils and fats.

8df09002a043.exp: Foams extinguish by smothering, forming a layer that isolates the fuel from oxygen, and by cooling, from the water they contain. They are useful for class A and B fires.

4b93bc1ac787.exp: Fires of cooking oils and fats, such as the vegetable oil in a frying pan, are class F. They are not class B (flammable liquids) because they require specific agents, and must never be put out with water.

6688bd7790ff.exp: After a collision, the priority is to investigate the seriousness of the damage (leaks, injured) before acting. Separating the vessels by going astern could worsen the damage, and distress messages or insurance details come afterwards, depending on severity.

ef220f372ee4.exp: When using flares the essential thing is that we can be seen: fire them only when someone is nearby who can detect them, in the right direction and with proper protection. It is not about using them up without judgement. The official answer is generic; it is also usual to show them to leeward.

0dafd4c28933.exp: For a nosebleed, keep the head tilted forward and press the nostrils for a few minutes. Tilting the head back makes the blood go down the throat, with a risk of nausea or aspiration.

de28f4c6c239.exp: To run aground (embarrancar) is for the vessel to be immobilised by having struck the bottom or a submerged obstacle. To collide (abordar) is to strike another vessel, and boarding is abordar in the sense of embarking.

49cf562de40f.exp: The smoke canister (orange smoke signal) is only useful by day, because at night the smoke cannot be seen. At night flares and luminous rockets are used. In fog it is not effective either.

c01e0ce51c66.exp: Blisters from sunburn are not drained, to avoid infection, and are covered with a greasy dressing. Draining them with a needle or squeezing them opens the door to infection.

fde27bb35ac9.exp: The telephone number of the Spanish Radio-Medical Centre is 913 103 475. It is a piece of data that must be memorised; do not confuse it with other similar numbers.

b7d8af716a9a.exp: To avoid a collision, safe speed is maintained at all times, which allows reacting and stopping in time according to the COLREGs. Lowering the navigation signals, disregarding equipment errors or putting out a buoy line (orinque) have nothing to do with avoiding collisions.

969ff698c57d.exp: After berthing, the seacocks are closed to guarantee watertightness and avoid a leak from a hose or fitting failure. The fuel ones have nothing to do with watertightness.

a997b7e6124d.exp: The most vulnerable points to a leak are the shaft passages through the hull: the rudder trunk (limera) and the propeller shaft tube (bocina), as well as the seacocks. Scuppers, hawse pipes or skylights are not the most critical.

d1af7a63dd81.exp: With the boat berthed and the engine stopped, the seacock is closed to prevent a leak. Leaving it open risks sinking if a hose or fitting fails.

31a6f55f0ef6.exp: Extinction by cooling consists of lowering the temperature of the fuel below its flash point, preventing the emission of combustible vapours. Dispersing is removing the fuel and interrupting the reaction is inhibition.

db79fef82de1.exp: Class B fire is produced by liquid fuels (petrol, diesel, oils). Class A: solids; C: gases; D: metals.

141dc9e7a46d.exp: For any burn, the immediate treatment is to cool with fresh or salt water for at least 10 minutes, to stop the damage. Ice, oil or creams are not applied, and blisters are not broken.

2aa0f05c760f.exp: For non-urgent or follow-up consultations, the CRME recommends calling between 09:00 and 15:00, when there is less care load. Emergencies are handled 24 hours.

a5561b130715.exp: For a fire to continue the four factors of the fire tetrahedron are required: fuel, oxidiser (oxygen), heat (activation energy) and chain reaction. Without the chain reaction it would be only the fire triangle, which explains the start.

2be588995737.exp: For combustion to start the fire triangle is enough: fuel, oxidiser and activation energy (heat). The chain reaction is added in the tetrahedron for the fire to continue.

f38eb6bebeee.exp: A leak (vía de agua) is an opening accidentally produced in the hull through which seawater enters. It is not the engine cooling water intakes, which are normal, controlled openings.

1b46ed8b5c9d.exp: In a severe airway obstruction (the casualty cannot cough or speak), up to 5 back blows are given between the shoulder blades and, if that does not work, you move on to the Heimlich manoeuvre (abdominal thrusts). One must not try to remove the object blindly with tweezers or needles.

a9f96e3f74fc.exp: A butane gas fire is extinguished by smothering with inert gas, depriving it of oxygen. First, if possible, shut off the gas outlet. Water or foam are not suitable for a gas fire.

0506f2e805d1.exp: When rafting up (abarloarse) alongside another boat that is berthed, you moor directly to her: the head lines go from our boat to the outer boat (bow and stern) and the springs and breast line to the same boat, not to the quay. That way the two boats form a unit and move together. Note: official key b says head lines to the quay, and that is what is accepted as correct in the question bank, although in practice the usual is what option c describes.
0506f2e805d1.duda: Possible error in the key: the normal practice when rafting up is to moor directly to the inside boat (option c) or, at most, head lines to the quay if possible; key b mixes both.

6119da583a83.exp: The wooden plug (espiche) is the conical wooden peg, nail-shaped, that is hammered in to temporarily plug a hole or leak. The collision mat or patch (turafalla), on the other hand, is a disc device with a threaded shaft and a folding piece; the clamp and the flange are fastening pieces, not plugs.

d4119727132b.exp: The wooden plug (espiche) is the conical wooden peg, nail-shaped, that is hammered in to temporarily plug a hole or leak. The collision mat or patch (turafalla), on the other hand, is a disc device with a threaded shaft and a folding piece; the clamp and the flange are fastening pieces, not plugs.

9483d6e5a95f.exp: For there to be fire, fuel, oxidiser (oxygen), heat and chain reaction are needed. To smother (sofocar) is to deprive the fire of the oxidiser: cover it with a fire blanket, close hatches or use CO2 or foam that displace oxygen. Removing the fuel is another method (isolation) and breaking the chain reaction is inhibition.

854b465d3ba7.exp: Fires are classified by the type of fuel: A solids (wood, cloth), B liquids (petrol, diesel, oils), C gases, D metals and F cooking oils and fats. Liquid fuel in tanks is a class B fire. Remember that A is solid and B is liquid.

99af16b5ebce.exp: In a flooding the urgent thing is to get out the water coming in to maintain buoyancy and stability, so the bilge pumps are started (while the leak is located and plugged). Going astern or increasing speed solves nothing and may worsen the water entry; three short blasts are not an action against flooding.

532a81e523c6.exp: When abandoning the vessel without a raft, the windward side (barlovento), from which the wind comes, is preferred, because that way the hull does not push us or fall on us, and we avoid flames and fumes if there is a fire. In addition, the drift then separates us from the vessel.
532a81e523c6.duda: Other questions from the same bank (72bae142e0dd) give leeward as correct for the same question; the key is contradictory between variants and the usual criterion depends on the situation (fire or not).

36ad381c3755.exp: When abandoning the vessel without a raft, the windward side (barlovento), from which the wind comes, is preferred, because that way the hull does not push us or fall on us, and we avoid flames and fumes if there is a fire. In addition, the drift then separates us from the vessel.
36ad381c3755.duda: Other questions from the same bank (72bae142e0dd) give leeward as correct for the same question; the key is contradictory between variants and the usual criterion depends on the situation (fire or not).

d9a090fb648d.exp: When abandoning the vessel without a raft, the windward side (barlovento), from which the wind comes, is preferred, because that way the hull does not push us or fall on us, and we avoid flames and fumes if there is a fire. In addition, the drift then separates us from the vessel.
d9a090fb648d.duda: Other questions from the same bank (72bae142e0dd) give leeward as correct for the same question; the key is contradictory between variants and the usual criterion depends on the situation (fire or not).

72bae142e0dd.exp: When abandoning the vessel over one side, the general rule is to do so to leeward (sotavento), which is the sheltered side: there is less swell, and the wind and drift do not push the vessel onto those in the water. Windward is chosen only in particular cases, such as a fire, to avoid flames and smoke.
72bae142e0dd.duda: Other variants of this question in the bank (532a81e523c6, 36ad381c3755, d9a090fb648d) give windward as correct; the key is inconsistent between variants.

8676da21df87.exp: With a burning gas leak, the first thing is to cut the supply by closing the stopcock or the cylinder valve, because that eliminates the fuel. Afterwards the fire can be fought with an extinguisher. Trying to cool with water or foam without cutting the gas is no use, since the gas would keep feeding the fire.

fa15f7e7e427.exp: Class A fires are those of solid fuels that leave embers, such as wood, paper, cloth or ropes. Mnemonic: A = solids (A for 'Ash'), B liquids, C gases, D metals.

8472fe8f45fb.exp: Class C fires are of gaseous fuels, such as butane or propane from the galley. Mnemonic: A solids, B liquids, C gases, D metals, F cooking oils and fats. Faced with them, the first thing is to cut the gas supply.

e00dd025c112.exp: Class F corresponds to cooking oil and fat fires (fryers, frying pans), which burn at very high temperatures and must not be put out with water. They are distinguished from B (flammable liquids such as petrol) and from A (solids).

0e7f4ef2f636.exp: Cooling with plenty of water (fresh or salt) for at least 10 minutes relieves pain and limits the depth of the injury. Ice, oil or ointments make the burn worse or retain heat, and blisters must not be pricked because they protect against infection.

2e9f8b9f5b5e.exp: The immediate treatment of any burn is to cool it as soon as possible, with saline solution or, if there is not enough, with water, for at least 10 minutes. Ice, oil or creams are counterproductive and blisters must not be broken, because they protect against the risk of infection.

066989e9ee51.exp: For a small burn, cool it straight away with cold water for a few minutes to reduce pain and injury. Ice, oil or ointments are not applied, and blisters, which protect the skin from infection, are not broken.

4a7ee875ea44.exp: Most collisions are avoided by keeping an effective look-out at all times (visual, aural and by radar if available), as Rule 5 of the COLREGs requires, and by complying with the steering and sailing rules. The other options are absurd or increase the risk.

22ea6dfa062a.exp: The preventive measure is to comply with the COLREGs (steering and sailing rules, lights, look-out, safe speed). Lowering the shapes, disregarding equipment errors or fastening the anchor with a buoy line (orincar) do not prevent collisions and even encourage them.

0d6b0bbced86.exp: A continuous fire requires four elements, the fire tetrahedron: fuel, oxidiser (oxygen), activation energy (heat) and chain reaction. If one is missing, the fire goes out. The classic triangle did not include the chain reaction, which is what sustains the fire once started.

e819ab9241e7.exp: The fire tetrahedron has four vertices: fuel, oxidiser (oxygen), activation energy (heat) and chain reaction. Removing any of them extinguishes the fire: cooling, smothering, isolation or inhibition. Hydrogen, air or fire are not elements of the tetrahedron.

6e71c53bb588.exp: For a nosebleed, keep the head tilted forward, so the blood comes out and is not swallowed or goes down the throat, and press the nostrils for 5 to 10 minutes. Tilting the head back is the typical mistake, since the blood goes down the throat and can cause vomiting.

3057f1f20cd0.exp: For a nosebleed, keep the head tilted forward, so the blood comes out and is not swallowed or goes down the throat, and press the nostrils for 5 to 10 minutes. Tilting the head back is the typical mistake, since the blood goes down the throat and can cause vomiting.

3d77eab08b51.exp: For a nosebleed, keep the head tilted forward, so the blood comes out and is not swallowed or goes down the throat, and press the nostrils for 5 to 10 minutes. Tilting the head back is the typical mistake, since the blood goes down the throat and can cause vomiting.

d2a6f4a90423.exp: Medical emergencies on board are consulted by radio with the Radio-Medical Centre of the Instituto Social de la Marina (ISM), in Madrid, which gives medical assistance and advice to vessels at sea. The Guardia Civil, the Harbour Master or a health clinic do not provide that radio-medical service.

f29bafc67a82.exp: Most collisions are due to human error: lack of look-out, excessive speed and failure to comply with the COLREGs. Efficient look-out, safe speed or correct stowage are just the opposite, measures that prevent them.

ba91e3111c6f.exp: Collisions occur mainly through human error and failure to comply with the COLREGs (poor look-out, not giving way, excessive speed). Efficient look-out and safe speed prevent collisions; sailing is not a cause of them.

75e1af3d39c4.exp: Skin reddened by the sun is a first-degree sunburn: it is treated with a moisturising cream or soothing lotion and by protecting from the sun. The casualty is not made to sweat with blankets, blisters are not burst and salt water irritates the skin.

33bd27ddf0de.exp: The rudder trunk (limera) is the opening through which the rudder stock (mecha) passes through the hull; it is a point vulnerable to leaks. The hawse pipe (gatera) is the opening for the anchor chain, the scupper (imbornal) drains the deck and the lead (escandallo) is the sounding weight.

7b97c45fc997.exp: The collision patch (turafalla) is the device for plugging a leak, made up of a felt or rubber disc with a threaded shaft and a folding element that opens inside the hull and is tightened from inside. The wooden plug (espiche) is a conical wooden peg, the collision mat (pallete de colisión) is a canvas with lines and the cleat (cornamusa) is for securing lines.

4836f8a3965c.exp: The collision patch (turafalla) is the device for plugging a leak, made up of a felt or rubber disc with a threaded shaft and a folding element that opens inside the hull and is tightened from inside. The wooden plug (espiche) is a conical wooden peg, the collision mat (pallete de colisión) is a canvas with lines and the cleat (cornamusa) is for securing lines.

c3f6299eb331.exp: Class B extinguishers are intended for fires of flammable liquids (petrol, diesel, oils, paints). They are not suitable for metals (class D) nor are they universal; for solids such as plastics class A is used, although ABC multipurpose powder covers several.

632c34e9d686.exp: The ISM radio-medical service gives medical assistance and advice to all ships at sea, of any nationality, and is completely free. It does not depend on whether we are sailing near the coast or on the flag.

0902848c6dd5.exp: After an unintentional grounding, the first thing is to inspect the hull, plug leaks and bail if necessary, and survey the bottom and surroundings. Going astern without knowing the state of the hull can worsen the damage or open a leak that the grounding itself was plugging.

9ef16ab66245.exp: When aground, the state of the bottom and possible hull damage must be analysed before manoeuvring. Going astern immediately may worsen the damage or sink the vessel if the grounding is plugging a leak. Marking the position with a buoy or preparing the sea anchor is not the first thing.

d193513d12e1.exp: In a radio-medical message the doctor is informed of the patient's condition: age, sex, pulse, breathing, temperature, blood pressure and symptoms. The Social Security membership number is not needed. That is why both A and C are correct.

9893403fd022.exp: Cooling consists of lowering the temperature of the fuel below its flash point, so that it no longer emits vapours that burn. It is achieved with water. The other options describe other methods: dispersion or removal of the fuel, and inhibition of the chemical reaction.

0c874fa808fb.exp: Smothering (sofocación) puts out the fire by eliminating the oxidiser, that is, oxygen, by means of fire blankets, CO2, foam or closing openings. Lowering the temperature is cooling and stopping the chemical reaction is inhibition.

d05bf3bfddd5.exp: The vessel is abandoned as a last resort, when she offers less safety than any other means of survival, for example a raft or dinghy. Being aground, an engine that will not start or uninjured crew do not justify abandoning the boat, which remains the best refuge.

102c3b0f16b8.exp: The tourniquet is the last resort for bleeding that does not stop by other means, and must not be kept tight for more than two hours at a stretch, as it can cause irreversible damage to the limb through lack of blood supply. The time of application must be noted.

696d697906fc.exp: The tourniquet is the last resort for severe bleeding from a limb. It may be kept tight for a maximum of two hours, because of the risk of injury from lack of blood supply. The time at which it was applied must be noted. It is not loosened every 15 minutes nor should its use be ruled out.

e9ba1d79b597.exp: For class A fires (solids such as wood or cloth) the ideal agent is water, which cools below the ignition temperature and penetrates the embers. CO2 and inert gases smother and foam works, but water is the most effective in this case.

ebead2f01f58.exp: The Spanish Radio-Medical Centre of the ISM handles medical consultations from vessels on the free telephone number 900 202 202 (also by radio). It is a piece of data worth memorising exactly for the exam.

8cd8e3e6eb63.exp: The false statement is C: seasickness (cinetosis) also affects experienced sailors, although they get used to it over time. The others are true: burns are classified from first to fourth degree, the ISM Radio-Medical Centre is in Madrid and after a collision the vessels must not be separated.

b08ee757eaba.exp: After a collision the priority is to assess the seriousness of the damage and of any leaks. The vessels are not separated before knowing it, because one may be plugging the hole in the other. Afterwards the engine is started and the incident is reported.

ddcf156f942a.exp: Arterial bleeding is the most serious: the blood is bright red (oxygenated) and spurts out, at the rhythm of the heartbeat. Venous blood is dark red and flows continuously and evenly.

51854a12534f.exp: The points of greatest risk of water entry are the openings in the hull: the shaft tube (bocina, passage of the propeller shaft), the rudder trunk (limera, passage of the rudder stock) and the seacocks. That is why it is advisable to check them and close the seacocks when not in use.

5cc3bfa009d4.exp: When firing signal rockets the essential thing is that we can be seen, so they are fired upward and the moment and direction are chosen when there are ships or land nearby. Firing them horizontally is dangerous and there is no fixed rule of bow or windward.

dff120aa6290.exp: When firing signal rockets the essential thing is that we can be seen, so they are fired upward and the moment and direction are chosen when there are ships or land nearby. Firing them horizontally is dangerous and there is no fixed rule of bow or windward.

810b64640332.exp: A leak (vía de agua) is an opening accidentally produced in the hull through which seawater enters. It is not a route, nor the engine cooling water inlet (which is a controlled intake), nor the place through which the bilge is pumped out.

89c5d438b667.exp: Water extinguishes mainly by cooling: it absorbs heat and lowers the temperature of the solid fuel below its ignition temperature. Smothering, by steam, is secondary. It does not inhibit the chain reaction (powders or halons do that) nor does it isolate or dilute the fuel.

41a4e09b9c84.exp: By day, 8 miles from the coast, the most effective means of attracting attention is the smoke canister, whose orange smoke is clearly seen in daylight. Rockets and flares are seen much better at night, and it is not advisable to use up all the material at once.

0c7f0f03dd83.exp: With the engine stopped, the seacock (cooling water intake valve) is closed to prevent a leak from a hose rupture or from siphoning if the intake is below the waterline. It has nothing to do with fuel or cooling.

4875ac8ae691.exp: Seacocks must be closed and opened frequently so they do not seize up from salt or encrustation, and can be closed in an emergency. They are kept closed when not in use, but opening and closing them periodically keeps them operational.

b7e95f9653b0.exp: In the northern hemisphere the wind turns clockwise around an anticyclone, flowing out from it. Around a depression it turns the other way. Mnemonic: anticyclone = clockwise; depression = anticlockwise.

eae89f971c88.exp: Depressions in the northern hemisphere generally move from west to east, carried by the mid-latitude westerlies. They do not change direction according to the day or the season.

0837af8fd808.exp: Anticyclones move more slowly than depressions and often remain almost stationary. Depressions move quickly from west to east. They are not totally static nor do they follow a fixed north-south direction.

6b816434b29d.exp: Isobars join points of equal pressure. When they are very close together, pressure changes a lot over a short distance (steep gradient) and therefore there is strong wind. Widely spaced isobars indicate light wind.

79eedbe8d231.exp: Wave height depends on three variables: the wind intensity, its persistence (hours blowing the same) and the fetch (distance over which it blows). Resistance, speed and durability are not the terms used.

b200d56def13.exp: The Douglas scale expresses the sea state (from 0 to 9) as a function of wave height; 'rough sea' (mar gruesa) is grade 6. The Beaufort scale measures wind force; Kelvin is for temperature and Williamson is a man-overboard manoeuvre.

cd258c10493b.exp: The sea state as a function of wave height is looked up on the Douglas scale. The Beaufort scale measures wind force, and persistence and the barometric scale are not sea-state scales.

f3466e1a6100.exp: The Douglas scale gives the name of the sea state (calm, rippled, smooth, slight, rough, etc.) and the wave height. Beaufort measures wind, Kelvin temperature and Williamson is a manoeuvre.

e05dcf79fcc1.exp: Isobars are the lines joining points of equal atmospheric pressure at a given moment. Isotherms join equal temperature, and isobaths equal depth. Mnemonic: 'baro' = pressure.

dd887d064699.exp: An isobaric line or isobar joins points of equal atmospheric pressure. Those joining points of equal depth are isobaths and those of equal magnetic variation are isogonic lines.

3b1a1ef50af1.exp: An isobar is the line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure ('baro' = pressure). Those of equal depth are isobaths and those of equal magnetic variation are isogonic lines.

837f65546798.exp: For the wind to veer or back (rolar) is for it to change direction: if clockwise, it veers to the right, and if anticlockwise, to the left. It does not refer to its intensity (that is freshening or moderating).

419485fef821.exp: The term applied to a change in wind direction is to veer or back (rolar). To freshen (refrescar) is to increase its force; to tack (virar) and to gybe (trasluchar) are manoeuvres of the boat, not of the wind.

5f375adb4d64.exp: The sea breeze (virazón) is the daytime breeze, from sea to land. By day the land heats up faster than the sea, the hot air rises over it and the cooler air from the sea comes in to take its place. At night the opposite occurs and the land breeze (terral) results.

bab7de85b71d.exp: In the northern hemisphere winds turn anticlockwise around a centre of low pressure (and flow in toward the centre). Mnemonic: depression = anticlockwise, anticyclone = clockwise.

3d2b79ca6dee.exp: In a northern hemisphere depression the wind turns anticlockwise, converging toward the centre. In the anticyclone it is the opposite, clockwise.

5473c2694a23.exp: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air above the Earth's surface (per unit area). The other options speak of the weight of the water contained in the air, which would be humidity, or give a column of incorrect dimensions.

18cc2df95056.exp: The aneroid barometer measures pressure by the deformation of a closed, evacuated metal capsule or box, with no liquid. The mercury one is based on the height of a column of mercury. Isobaric and alcohol are not types of barometer.

2e383c5d46e1.exp: Wind intensity is a speed and is measured in knots (nautical miles per hour). Among the options, the only unit of speed is miles per hour.
2e383c5d46e1.duda: Strictly the unit is knots (nautical miles per hour); 'miles per hour' is imprecise, but it is the only option that expresses speed.

ebc822e20ae2.exp: Wind intensity is its speed, which is measured in knots (nautical miles per hour) or in m/s. Therefore it is measured in units of speed, not of pressure, length or time.

4a79a1858a95.exp: Persistence is the number of hours the wind has blown in the same direction and with the same intensity. Together with intensity and fetch it determines wave height. Fetch is distance, not time.

73932a84523e.exp: The land breeze (terral) is the night wind that blows from land toward the sea. At night the land cools more than the sea and the cool air descends toward the warmer water. Its opposite is the sea breeze (virazón), daytime and from sea to land.

19472adc4992.exp: The sea breeze (virazón) blows during the day, from sea to land, because the land heats up before the sea and draws in cooler air. Mnemonic: virazón by day, terral by night.

8ecb0df946ff.exp: The coastal breezes are the sea breeze (virazón; daytime, from sea to land) and the land breeze (terral; nighttime, from land to sea). The other options are invented names.

d48f47430580.exp: An anticyclone is an area of high pressure, where the air descends and moves away from the centre, and usually gives good weather. It is not defined by temperature but by pressure; the area of low pressure is a depression.

402fefd1dae8.exp: An atmospheric low or depression (borrasca) is an area of low pressure where the air rises and converges toward the centre, and usually brings bad weather. It is not defined by temperature or by precipitation.

00d402650431.exp: The Beaufort scale estimates wind force from its effects, from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane). Douglas is for sea state, Saffir-Simpson classifies hurricanes by categories and Venturi is a physical effect.
00d402650431.duda: Option d appears with erroneous text ('x UT10 Teoria de navegació...'); the real answer, Beaufort, is not among the options.

0405df3d9944.exp: Fetch is the distance over which the wind blows unobstructed, and is measured in nautical miles. Hours measure persistence and knots measure wind speed.

237189dbf18d.exp: Fetch is the stretch of sea over which the wind blows in a constant direction, so it is measured in nautical miles. Hours measure persistence and knots measure wind speed.

d69e624f0fdc.exp: Fetch is the extent (distance) over which a wind of constant direction and speed blows; the greater it is, the bigger the waves. Direction, intensity and time (which is persistence) are other factors.

d0dff0465173.exp: Normal atmospheric pressure at sea level is 760 mm Hg, equivalent to 1013.2 hPa (or mb). Not to be confused with 1013, which is the value in hectopascals.

ed73ffb104fc.exp: Normal pressure at sea level is 1013.2 hectopascals (hPa), equivalent to 760 mm Hg. Mnemonic: 1013 hPa = 760 mmHg.

31ce207bcc55.exp: One hectopascal equals 0.75 mm of mercury, since 1013.2 hPa is 760 mm Hg (760/1013 is approximately 0.75). A millibar is the same as a hectopascal.

0af98aa4f057.exp: For the wind to freshen (refrescar) is for its intensity to increase gradually. To gust (rachear) is to blow in gusts, to veer or back (rolar) is to change direction and to ease (recalmar) is to decrease its force.

a1237873573c.exp: For the wind to freshen (refrescar) means its force increases, and gradually. To decrease is to moderate or ease (amainar or recalmar), and to change direction is to veer or back (rolar).

b491a7465386.exp: In the northern hemisphere the wind turns clockwise around an anticyclone, flowing out from it. In a depression it is the opposite. Mnemonic: anticyclone = clockwise.

c49c19c66bd4.exp: With the boat at anchor there is no way on, so the wind felt on board is the true wind. When the boat moves, her own speed combines with the true wind and the apparent wind is felt.

396daa3f0cd8.exp: With way on, the wind felt on board is the apparent wind, the result of combining the true wind with the wind created by the boat's movement. Without way, the apparent wind coincides with the true wind.

5395a2f00964.exp: The anemometer measures wind speed. The wind vane indicates its direction, and ventímetro and velocímetro are not meteorological instruments for this use. Mnemonic: 'anemo' = wind.

17e548acbc86.exp: At anchor there is no way on, so the apparent wind equals the true wind, and the anemometer shows its speed in knots: 15 knots. It does not indicate direction, and it is not 1.5 knots.

7afb262fc05b.exp: At anchor there is no way on, so the apparent wind coincides with the true wind and the anemometer indicates its speed in knots: 13 knots. It does not give direction nor is it expressed in km/h.

65d00c4658d5.exp: Air moves from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas, seeking to equalise them; that is wind. That is why barometer readings are related to wind, and the greater the difference, the stronger it blows.

9d6ed1078f8b.exp: The instrument for measuring atmospheric pressure is the barometer (aneroid or mercury). The thermometer measures temperature, the anemometer wind speed and the thermograph records temperatures.

be592f98ca8e.exp: The Celsius or centigrade scale sets 0 ºC at the freezing of water and 100 ºC at its boiling at 1 atm. Fahrenheit uses 32 and 212 ºF; Douglas and Beaufort are not temperature scales.

3c6d05ee781e.exp: Fetch is the straight-line distance over which the wind blows unobstructed, so it is a length. It is measured in nautical miles (or km), not in hours or knots. Together with intensity and persistence it determines wave height: the greater the fetch, the bigger the waves.

ec94afaee401.exp: Persistence is the time during which the wind blows with the same direction and intensity, so it is measured in hours. Fetch, by contrast, is a distance and intensity is a speed (knots). The longer the wind persists, the more the waves grow.

e2665c22bf7e.exp: The sea breeze (virazón) is the daytime breeze: during the day the land heats up faster than the sea, the warm air over the land rises and the cooler air from the sea comes toward the coast. It blows from sea to land, perpendicular to the coast. At night the opposite happens and it is the land breeze (terral).

ce10a58b9487.exp: To veer or back (rolar) is for the wind to change direction (for example, from NE to E). Not to be confused with freshening (increasing in intensity) or easing or calming (decreasing in intensity). Rolar always refers to direction; freshening and calming, to force.

f5a50de57da6.exp: On the Celsius (centigrade) scale the melting point of ice at 1 atm is 0 ºC and the boiling of water 100 ºC. Fahrenheit (32 ºF) and Kelvin (273.15 K) use other origins. Douglas and Beaufort are not temperature scales but sea and wind scales.

3a43f363ef0e.exp: A gust is a sudden, brief increase in wind intensity, normally lasting a few seconds. That is why gusty wind is variable in force. It is not the same as freshening, which is a sustained increase in intensity.

461d8732a1de.exp: Isobars are the lines on weather maps that join points of equal atmospheric pressure. Not to be confused with isobaths (equal depth), isotherms (equal temperature) or isogonic lines (equal magnetic variation). Mnemonic: iso-BAR, from barometer.

b72dbbfaa7d5.exp: The height of wind waves (mar de viento) depends on three factors: intensity (wind force), persistence (hours it blows) and fetch (distance over which it blows). Mnemonic: IPF. If any of the three is missing, wave size is limited; latitude, temperature or isobars are not direct factors.

0c4a2cda9670.exp: In the northern hemisphere the wind turns around a depression (low pressure) anticlockwise and inward, toward the centre. In the anticyclone it is the opposite: clockwise and outward. Mnemonic: lows turn 'against the clock'.

f9d47f328ea8.exp: Normal atmospheric pressure at sea level and 0 ºC is 1013.2 mbar = 1013.2 hPa (equivalent to 760 mm Hg). Hectopascals and millibars are the same unit. The other values do not correspond to any equivalence of normal pressure.

661dd202d189.exp: The anemometer measures wind speed (intensity), normally in knots. For direction the wind vane or the telltale (cataviento) is used; for pressure, the barometer; for humidity, the hygrometer.

2cf57627ab63.exp: The height of wind waves (mar de viento) depends on three factors: intensity (wind force), persistence (hours it blows) and fetch (distance over which it blows). Mnemonic: IPF. If any of the three is missing, wave size is limited; latitude, temperature or isobars are not direct factors.

33e34e5a5556.exp: The aneroid barometer measures atmospheric pressure by means of a metal capsule that deforms with pressure. Temperature is read on the thermometer, relative humidity on the hygrometer or psychrometer. Its variations serve to forecast the weather.

2a1e3e3872b8.exp: A sharp fall of the barometer indicates a depression is approaching: the wind will increase and precipitation and worsening weather are likely. A rise in pressure would be the opposite, stable weather typical of an anticyclone. That is why the barometer is key for forecasting weather on board.

fe1e3cc33265.exp: In the northern hemisphere the wind turns around a depression (low pressure) anticlockwise and inward, toward the centre. In the anticyclone it is the opposite: clockwise and outward. Mnemonic: lows turn 'against the clock'.

fefb5a09bcb7.exp: To freshen (refrescar) is to increase the wind intensity (the wind freshens). To calm is the opposite, to decrease; to veer or back (rolar) is to change direction. To gust (rachear) is not the action of increasing in a sustained way: a gust is a sudden, momentary increase.

3c92db18d809.exp: The land breeze (terral) blows from land to sea during the night: the land cools faster than the sea, the air over the sea stays warmer and rises, and the cold air from the land moves toward the sea. It is the inverse effect of the daytime sea breeze (virazón).

7970ea895f4d.exp: Wind intensity is measured in knots (nautical miles per hour), and the Beaufort scale classifies it. Bar is a unit of pressure, the mile is of distance and revolutions per minute are for the engine.

a623e9af255d.exp: Fetch is the straight-line distance over which the wind blows unobstructed, so it is a length. It is measured in nautical miles (or km), not in hours or knots. Together with intensity and persistence it determines wave height: the greater the fetch, the bigger the waves.

4427a4fb5e4d.exp: To forecast the weather on board, the barometer, which reports pressure and its trends, and the thermometer, which gives the temperature, are used. The wind vane and the anemometer indicate the current wind direction and speed, and do not help to predict. A fall in pressure together with a drop in temperature announces worsening.

380c1c8a4eeb.exp: The sea breeze (virazón) is the daytime breeze: during the day the land heats up faster than the sea, the warm air over the land rises and the cooler air from the sea comes toward the coast. It blows from sea to land, perpendicular to the coast. At night the opposite happens and it is the land breeze (terral).

61682b0e075d.exp: True wind (viento real) is the one we feel with the boat not making way, stopped or at anchor. When sailing the boat also generates a relative wind and what we perceive is the apparent wind, the sum of true and relative. Supposed wind and compass wind are not types of wind.

6d6cd9638e80.exp: Fetch is the straight stretch of sea over which a wind of constant direction and intensity blows. It is a distance (miles), not a time: do not confuse it with persistence, which is the hours the wind blows. Fetch, intensity and persistence determine wind waves (mar de viento).
